long.title: Animals Thought Extinct Found Alive (One Was Hiding on a Rock for 80 Years)
tags: extinct animals that were found alive
long.comment: 🦤 Best answer gets read out in the next episode: which extinct animal would you bring back, and why?
long.description: Can an animal really come back from extinction? These did. A fish that was supposed to have died with the dinosaurs, a coelacanth found at a fish market on a honeymoon, a bird that hid for 50 years, a ferret rediscovered by a ranch dog named Shep, and a giant insect hiding on a sea cliff for 80 years. Meatball tells the whole story. Which extinct animal would you bring back? Best answer gets read out next time 👇 0:00 Cold open 0:38 The fish older than dinosaurs 1:46 The honeymoon fish 2:20 The bird gone for 50 years 3:14 The ferret a dog found 4:33 The insect on the rock 5:42 Adam and Eve 6:18 So, what's the lesson? Tuesday: another weird true story. shorts.title: The Fish That Was 'Extinct' for 66 Million Years 🐟
shorts.description:
This fish died out with the dinosaurs. At least, that's what every scientist on Earth thought, until 1938. Its genus, Latimeria, is named after the museum curator who spotted it.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: He Found a 'Dinosaur Fish' on His Honeymoon 🐟
shorts.description:
A biologist found a brand new species of coelacanth on his honeymoon. At a fish market. For sale. A second Indonesian coelacanth was caught by local fishermen in July 1998.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: This Bird Was 'Extinct' for 50 Years 🐦
shorts.description:
This bird was declared extinct in 1898. Fifty years later, a doctor followed some footprints up a mountain in New Zealand, and found it. Today there are around 500 takahē, and the number is slowly growing.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: A Dog Found This 'Extinct' Animal 🐾
shorts.description:
This ferret was declared extinct in 1979. Two years later, a ranch dog in Wyoming named Shep brought one home. Biologists then found a colony of more than 100 black-footed ferrets near Meeteetse, Wyoming.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: This Insect Hid on a Rock for 80 Years 🪲
shorts.description: This insect was declared extinct after rats took over its island. Eighty years later, scientists found it clinging to a sea cliff, under one single bush. The rock is Ball's Pyramid, about 23 km from Lord Howe Island, Australia. #shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Lord Howe Island stick insect: "Our Wondrous Planet, Our Wild Family: Dry Specimen - Lord Howe Island stick insect, Dryococelus australis Montrouzier, 1855" by Photographer: Benjamin Healley (CC BY 4.0), via museumsvictoria, "Our Wondrous Planet, Our Wild Family: Dry Specimen - Lord Howe Island stick insect, Dryococelus australis Montrouzier, 1855" by Photographer: Thomas Breakwell (CC BY 4.0), via museumsvictoria; Ball's Pyramid: "Ball's Pyramid" by sbittinger (CC BY 2.0), via flickr. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0

shorts.title: One Pair of Bugs Saved a Whole Species 🪲
shorts.description: In 2003, scientists took two pairs off the rock. One pair went to Melbourne Zoo, where keepers named them Adam and Eve. Almost every tree lobster at the zoo comes from that one pair. Zoos in Europe and North America now breed them too. #shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Lord Howe Island stick insect: "Our Wondrous Planet, Our Wild Family: Dry Specimen - Lord Howe Island stick insect, Dryococelus australis Montrouzier, 1855" by Photographer: Thomas Breakwell (CC BY 4.0), via museumsvictoria, "Our Wondrous Planet, Our Wild Family: Dry Specimen - Lord Howe Island stick insect, Dryococelus australis Montrouzier, 1855" by Photographer: Benjamin Healley (CC BY 4.0), via museumsvictoria. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
